key_idea: Sort the queried strings lexicographically; a prefix is an ancestor of exactly L of them iff it covers a window of L consecutive strings, so each window contributes max(0, lcp(window ends) - max(lcp with left neighbour, lcp with right neighbour)).
sketch: Sort all N strings once, compute the LCP of lexicographically adjacent strings directly (total cost bounded by total length), and build a sparse table so lcp(rank a, rank b) is a range minimum in O(1); lcp of a string with itself is its length. For each query map the K ids to ranks, sort them, and slide a window of size L: prefixes of length in (max(lcp(v[i-1],v[i]), lcp(v[i+L-1],v[i+L])), lcp(v[i],v[i+L-1])] are exactly those covering precisely that window. Total O((sum len + N) log N + sum K log K). Pitfalls: L = 1 (window lcp is the string length), boundaries of the window at the ends of the list, and 64-bit answers. Verified against a brute force on small random inputs.
